#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   -n 4
#   --mem 2000
#   -p mlow,mlow
#   --gres gpu:1
#   -o logs/%x_%u_%j.out
#   -e logs/%x_%u_%j.err

#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 4
#flux: -c 1

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem 2000
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on a node with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm option: --gres gpu:1
# Flux GPU requests are site/config dependent (often via custom resource types).
# Performance implication: job may start without a GPU, causing failure or severe slowdown.

# Omitted Slurm option: -p mlow,mlow (partition)
# Flux queues/partitions are site-specific; no portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: job may run with different limits/priority or be rejected by policy.

# Omitted Slurm options: -o/-e with %x/%u/%j tokens
# Slurm tokens are not portable in Flux output/error directives.
# Performance implication: none, but logs may overwrite/collide unless you choose unique filenames.

# Slurm requested 4 tasks; preserve by launching under Flux.
flux run -n 4 -c 1 python metric_learning.py --arch-type siamese --epochs 200 --process eval

reasons: The original Slurm job required 1 GPU (`--gres gpu:1`) but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this may allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run much slower.
The original Slurm job requested memory (`--mem 2000`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this may under-provision the job and risk OOM.

The original Slurm job specified a partition (`-p mlow,mlow`) but the Flux resource section has no queue/partition selection; on sites where this affects eligibility/limits, scheduling behavior may differ or the job may be rejected.

#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH -n 4 # Number of cores
#SBATCH --mem 2000 # 2GB solicitados.
#SBATCH -p mlow,mlow # or mlow Partition to submit to master low prioriy queue
#SBATCH --gres gpu:1 # Para pedir Pascales MAX 8
#SBATCH -o logs/%x_%u_%j.out # File to which STDOUT will be written
#SBATCH -e logs/%x_%u_%j.err # File to which STDERR will be written
python metric_learning.py --arch-type siamese --epochs 200 --process eval
